To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel redundantly actuated 6RSS parallel robot with two higher kinematic pairs is developed to emulate the complex mandibular movements, and a distributed-torque-based independent joint control is proposed to enhance the motion tracking accuracy.
a redundantly actuated robot of the 5RSSR mechanism with two HKPs can be controlled to emulate complex mandible motions with high accuracy.
the proposed robot can be used as an experimental platform to investigate the masticatory process, and that the developed control algorithms can enhance the motion tracking performance of the robot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and control of a novel parallel robot that can be used to investigate human chewing motions in the laboratory.

the development of a novel parallel robot for the evaluation of the masticatory function, which is able to mimic the complex human mandibular movement and can provide a quantitative assessment of food texture.
the design, modeling, control, and evaluation of a novel redundantly actuated 6RSS parallel robot for the evaluation of masticatory biomechanics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed control algorithms have the capability to improve the performance of the robot and the robot has the capability to reproduce human mandibular motions.
the distributed-torque control is effective in improving the independent joint motion tracking of the redundantly actuated robot.

the distributed torque is an effective feedforward to enhance independent joint control, especially for the robot with higher kinematic pairs, and the frictional effects can be compensated for to further enhance the tracking accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robot has been developed to a stage where it can be employed to investigate the mastication process.
the robot is capable of mimicking the human chewing motion with a high level of accuracy, and it is a promising device for food texture evaluation.
the robot can be a promising tool for the evaluation of the texture change during mastication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed robot and control algorithms have the potential to be utilized as a biomimetic tool to study human mastication.
the robot can be used for the evaluation of mastication-related food texture changes in a biomimicry manner.
a redundant parallel robot with two HKPs is capable of reproducing complex motions, and the distributed-torque joint control can be applied to enhance the tracking performance.
